BLOCKER: AC contradiction: Round-4 removed the ATTACH event trigger, yet an AC demands "a test proves a direct attach cannot leave a leaf without RLS/deny_mutation"; the design itself concedes a privileged ATTACH can create an unhardened leaf. Either the AC is restated (attach denied to app/runtime roles + assert detects privileged attach) or an enforcement mechanism is added — AC is not demonstrably met as written.

Sequence identity is inconsistent: Phase 1 §3 says "CREATE SEQUENCE audit_id_seq", while the AC/hardening text requires setval on "audit_new_id_seq" and --down "recreates audit_id_seq". Two names for one object means migration, tool and tests cannot all satisfy the AC; pin one canonical name in the AC and DDL.
MAJOR: Swap-tool crash recovery beyond S2 is undefined: a crash after the S4 rename commits but before state/post-swap verification, or a reconnect mid-rename, has no resume/idempotent re-entry rule or failure-injection test (guardrail 6 requires migration-interrupted recovery).

Lock acquisition under lock_timeout=3s can fail with 55P03; the AC's 5-attempt/1-2-4-8-16s retry loop only covers a delta overflow. Specify 55P03 handling, else a contended swap exits without a defined path.

Backup scope is underspecified: `pg_dump -t audit` must explicitly capture the id sequence, table DEFAULT, triggers, grants and dependent views; restore row count alone does not prove rollback completeness. Enumerate dumped objects in S1 verification.

Legal hold placed after PURGE is unhandled: "hold on an archived month blocks purge" only protects until purge_grace_days elapses. Need an invariant that a HOLD cannot be recorded against a purged month (or an immediate spoliation alert + documented residual risk).

Grants on audit_legal_hold_archive are not stated: if no tenant SELECT grant, held rows become unreadable to tenants post-drop; if granted, the cross-tenant test must cover this table as "any path". Declare the grant set explicitly.

AC privilege model vs deny_mutation: TRUNCATE coverage needs both an explicit TRUNCATE privilege revocation statement and proof the TRUNCATE trigger fires on the partitioned parent and leaves; trigger-only coverage is convention, contradicting "enforced by privilege".
MINOR: Fast-path wording: a plpgsql BEFORE trigger uses SPI-cached plans, not "prepared statements"; ensure the implementation avoids EXECUTE (no plan reuse) so the config-update test's "applies immediately" claim holds.

audit_insert_out_of_range_total is only incremented by AuditStore.Append; non-Go writers (psql, other services) fail closed silently with no telemetry — document the residual blind spot or add a DB-side signal.

audit_late_YYYYMM partitions are excluded from coverage and created outside the grace/monthly span; state their range invariant (strictly below grace, non-overlapping) and confirm test globs (`audit_%`) don't conflate them with monthly partitions.

Language rule: audit_ensure_partitions, audit_hold_extract, audit_append_late and the provisioning trigger are shipped logic in plpgsql; ensure the ADR explicitly blesses these as single-purpose primitives (CL-001/CL-008) rather than leaving it implicit.
Append-only enforcement for audit_migration_state_events / audit_legal_hold_events is asserted but the mechanism (revokes vs trigger) is unstated; pf_owner could still UPDATE/DELETE.
Re-run of 0014 after months elapse: idempotency must be ensure-based (never drop/recreate existing partitions or re-setval a live sequence); state this so "idempotent" is testable.
NIT: Rollback naming: AC says --down "recreates audit_id_seq" while Phase 1 creates a sequence that later drops with audit_legacy — use one naming table in docs/ADR.
purge_grace_days=90 vs rollback_window_days=14 vs legal retention: pin the relationship (backup retention >= legal retention) in one config block to avoid drift.
Operator approval for purge needs actor attribution (who, when, reason) defined as a recorded field, not just a CLI flag.
SUMMARY: Solid, defense-in-depth design (privilege-enforced hardening, bounded freeze, two-stage retention, append-only state), but two AC-level defects block Gate 1: the unachievable "direct attach cannot leave an unhardened leaf" criterion and the audit_id_seq/audit_new_id_seq naming split.
Top risks: swap-tool crash resume after rename, hold-after-purge spoliation gap, backup object completeness, and lock-timeout retry semantics — none has a stated invariant plus test yet.
